candidates.change_summary: Change returned selector to a different constant (returning 0x0 instead of the selector), causing onERC721Received to return a different value.
Return the bitwise-inverted selector value (flip all bits), producing a different bytes4 return value.
Return the zeroed selector of a different function (onERC721Received.selector of a new temporary interface) to alter returned bytes4 value.
Replace assignment to baseToken with assigning address(0) unconditionally, changing stored baseToken value regardless of _baseToken argument.
Replace assignment to baseToken with assigning msg.sender, causing baseToken to be the initializer rather than the provided _baseToken.
Replace assignment to baseToken with assigning _nft (swapping values), causing baseToken to be set to the nft argument.
Delete the assignment to baseToken, leaving it unchanged from its previous value.
Insert an extra assignment setting baseToken = address(this) after the original assignment, overriding the provided _baseToken.
Replace assignment to nft with assigning the zero address so initialize sets nft = address(0) instead of provided _nft.
Replace assignment to nft with assigning baseToken so initialize sets nft to the baseToken address provided.
Replace assignment to nft with assigning msg.sender so initialize sets nft to the caller address instead of provided _nft.
Replace assignment to changeFee with assigning twice the provided _changeFee (changing stored value).
Replace assignment to changeFee with assigning zero regardless of provided _changeFee.
Replace assignment to changeFee with assigning the provided _changeFee plus one (off-by-one change).
Remove the feeRate upper-bound check so any _feeRate is accepted (deleting the revert on >5000).
Invert the fee-rate validation to revert if _feeRate is <= 5000, allowing only values >5000 (changes stored feeRate for many inputs).
Change assignment to set feeRate to zero regardless of _feeRate (makes observed feeRate always 0 after initialize).
Change the check that prevents re-initialization from reverting to instead allowing re-initialization by removing the revert on already-initialized (replace the initial if check to do nothing).

Invert the AlreadyInitialized check so initialize can only be called if already initialized (i.e., require initialized is true), causing initialized to remain true but preventing the first initialization from succeeding.
Move the line setting initialized = true to be executed before assigning other state variables (so initialized becomes true earlier during initialization).
